conviction_note: abs_move 4.0 comes from Vesta's own last four confirmed release reactions (+5.0, +6.9, +2.3, -1.0), which I rebuilt because the baseline history is monthly 6-Ks. p_up 56 is a mild lean: H1 run-rate makes a guidance raise likely, but the street can see that arithmetic, the stock is +10% over 20 days and 2.6% off its 52-week high, and the peer read is mixed. impact_sum +0.6 and the scaled +0.48 agree in sign and size.
bar: Company 2026 guide: rental revenues +10.0-11.0% on FY2025 US$273.6m, so US$301.0-303.7m. Adjusted NOI margin ~93.5%, adjusted EBITDA margin ~83% (Q4 2025 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1969373/000196937326000006/quarterlyreport4q2025ex-991.htm). H1 2026 ex-energy was US$150.0m (74.0 + 76.0), so the guide implies about US$75.5-76.9m per quarter in H2. I expect Q3 at about US$78-79m, roughly +3% over that implied run-rate. The street Q3 consensus is unsourced: Earnings Whispers shows a $0.30 EPS that is IFRS and revaluation-driven, and the four-analyst revenue/FFO consensus was not found. So print_vs_bar is measured against the company guide, not the street.
positioning_check: No options market (baseline options.status no_options_market), so no skew. VTMX ADR short interest 546.9k shares, 5.09 days to cover, 2026-06-30 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/vtmx/, updated 2026-07-14). Equibles: 241.8k shares, 2.31 DTC on 2026-03-13. That is a small fraction of the roughly 94m ADS-equivalents the ~940m shares imply, so not a crowded short. No October figure found. Run-up: +3.4% over 5 days, +9.97% over 20 days, 2.6% below the 52-week high. Coverage is thin, about 4 analysts; consensus PT was $42 at 2026-06-30 per vcpscanner.

findings.finding: Vesta's 2026 guide (rental revenues +10-11% to about US$301-304m) was left unchanged at Q2 although H1 ex-energy revenue was US$150.0m (+15.2% YoY: Q1 +14.1%, Q2 +16.2%). Q2 ended at 91.7% occupancy (+200bp QoQ), so Q3 should step up sequentially from US$76.0m, and the year tracks about +12-13% against the 10-11% guide. The arithmetic points to a raise, or at least 'top end', on 2026-10-22, the first chance after the occupancy step-up. Last year's Q3 release raised the EBITDA margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-10-23 amc): 2025 EBITDA margin guide raised to 84.5% from 83.5%, stock 27.41 to 28.77 (+5.0%). Q4 2025 (2026-02-19 amc): 2025 revenue above the top of guide plus the first 2026 guide, 33.67 to 35.99 (+6.9%). Q2 2026 (2026-07-22 amc): guide maintained, 34.03 to 33.69 (-1.0%). Closes from the Yahoo chart https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/VTMX?range=1y&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 numbers are public, so sell-side models with four analysts probably already sit above the guide, and that part is priced. What is not priced is whether management converts it: it held the guide at Q2 ('I feel comfortable with the guidance'). If the market had fully priced a raise, the Q2 print would not have been sold (-1.0%) and the stock would not have sat flat at $33-34 from July to early October. The +10% run-up since about 10-09 is partly this, so the finding is sized below the median reaction.
findings.independence: Guide text from a different document, the Q4 2025 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1969373/000196937326000006/quarterlyreport4q2025ex-991.htm. Q2 call transcript (management comfortable with the guide, analyst notes H1 ahead of it): https://www.webull.com/news/15277439136130048

findings.finding: Direct peer FIBRA Prologis reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-21 after the close, the first Mexican industrial landlord to speak since Vesta's July print. Period-end occupancy rose to 96.5% from 95.8% at Q2. The CEO cited 'improving customer demand and lower construction starts'. Against that, same-store cash NOI was +1.7% vs +14.8% a year earlier, average occupancy 95.1% vs 97.9%, rent change on rollover 36.2% vs 47.2%, and retention 66.0% vs 81.7%. Net, a mildly positive demand read on occupancy direction with decelerating rent momentum.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of VTMX reacting to FIBRA Prologis prints. VTMX was 36.20 on 10-21 and 35.99 intraday on 10-22 (partial session, 19k volume), so there was no visible positive reaction to the peer release.
findings.why_not_priced: It was public about 18 hours before the print and VTMX traded through it, so most of it is priced; the flat-to-down 10-22 tape shows the market did not treat it as a strong read-through. The residual is that Vesta (91.7% occupancy, more lease-up room than FIBRAPL) gets more leverage from improving demand than the 96% peer shows.
findings.independence: Proxy (peer, not Vesta's own number). Same direction from CBRE Q2 2026 local data: Monterrey vacancy down 10bp QoQ to 6.8%, Juárez vacancy down 80bp QoQ (summarised via https://clusterindustrial.com.mx/monterrey-suma-casi-18-millones-de-m2-industriales-y-mantiene-crecimiento-sostenido-cbre/). Weak.

findings.finding: The May 2026 global offering (about 77.8m new share-equivalents: 58.05m common + 1.97m ADSs x 10, roughly +9% on the Q1 average 859.0m shares, about US$269m gross) lands for a full quarter in Q3. Q2 already showed Vesta FFO per share -1.8% YoY and FFO after tax per share -26.2% with only part of a quarter of dilution, so Q3 FFO per share is likely flat-to-down YoY against Q3 2025's US$47.4m FFO on about 868m shares. The money funds a 1.78m sf development pipeline at a 10.1% expected yield (22.3% pre-leased) plus land, so it is growth funding, not distress.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (first per-share dilution print, FFO/share -1.8%): -1.0%. Q1 2026 (FFO -4.1% YoY on lower interest income): +2.3%. This name has not been punished hard on FFO per share.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the share count and the Q2 per-share decline are public. What is left is the size of a full-quarter per-share decline on a name that trades on FFO yield, at a moment when the stock has run up into the print.
findings.independence: Same document as finding 1 (Q2 6-K), used for a different line (per-share vs revenue). Share count for Q1 from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001969373/000196937326000013/quarterlyreport1q2026ex-991.htm

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 Vesta prepaid US$105m of private debt early (US$60m 5.31% notes due 2027-09, US$45m 5.85% term loan due 2028-05), paying make-whole amounts in Q3. That puts a one-off finance charge, not quantified in the release, into Q3, and removes about US$5.8m a year of interest from Q4 on. S&P (2026-08-21) and Fitch (2026-08-31) both upgraded Vesta to BBB/stable. Financing question answered: the cash comes from the May equity raise and the move simplifies the structure. It is not distress, so this nets to about zero.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. The 6-K days after the upgrades and the prepayment moved -1.2% (08-24), -0.58% (08-31) and +0.24% (09-09) per the baseline's non-earnings rows.
findings.why_not_priced: The make-whole cost is unquantified and will appear in Q3 finance costs, a below-operating-income one-off, so it can blur the reported FFO by a cent-fraction. The rating upgrades and the prepayment themselves are public and priced.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: VTMX rose from 33.87 (10-09) to 36.72 (10-20) and sat at 35.99 on 10-22, +9.97% over 20 sessions and 2.6% below its 52-week high, on thin ADR turnover (about 64k shares a day per the baseline). A good part of a positive print is in the price; the last print with no guide change was sold -1.0%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a flat tape and fell -1.0%. Q4 2025 came after a flat tape (33.6-33.7) and rose +6.9%. No case in the sample of a print following a 10% run-up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, not an unpriced fact. It is filed to offset the guidance finding: the run-up is what pricing-in of a raise would look like.

findings.finding: Inside Q2, which the CEO letter did not discuss, Bajío stabilized occupancy fell from 96.0% to 92.2%, Bajío same-store from 95.8% to 94.2%, North same-store from 97.1% to 93.0%, and Bajío vacant sf rose to 2.11m (10.3%), while total occupancy rose on lease-up of new product. If those regional slides continue in Q3, same-store NOI growth (+5.9% in Q2) and the occupancy headline could disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, the print that carried these declines, moved -1.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the July filing's tables, not in the wire copy or the call summaries, which led with the +200bp total occupancy. Segment net of the rest: Monterrey (>80%), Mexico City and Central SE (100%) and new deliveries carried the total, so this is sized small and net.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 3. FIBRA Prologis's weak same-store cash NOI of +1.7% in Q3 (finding 2's document) points the same way on same-store momentum.

findings.finding: The US did not extend USMCA and moves to annual reviews through 2036 (El CEO, 2026-10-06), with a USTR public consultation open to January. Vesta's Q2 letter already called the July 1 review 'continuity, but not resolution'. Management will be asked about tenant decision delays on the 10-23 call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 call flagged USMCA uncertainty and the stock moved -1.0%. The stock has risen about 10% since the 10-06 article, so the market has looked through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a macro headline every holder knows. The residual is any company-specific statement of leasing delays on the call. Macro-to-company transmission is not confirmed by the company, so this is a proxy.
findings.independence: Vesta Q2 6-K CEO letter ('continuity, but not resolution'): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001969373/000196937326000016/quarterlyreport2q2026ex-991.htm
